competitors.label: XMTD
competitors.headline: Up to USD 20 / lot
competitors.basis: Fixed fee or percentage per lot
competitors.japan: Japan-specific partner page and introducer agreement
competitors.economics: Up to USD 20/lot, unlimited commissions and a 10% sub-affiliate commission are advertised.
competitors.rebate: Cashback is mentioned on the partner page. The agreement requires written authorisation before passing introducer payments to third parties.
competitors.payout: Weekly; no payment below USD 500; USD only unless an alternative is approved.
competitors.restrictions: Trades held five minutes or less are excluded; bonus, churning, fraud and self-referral controls apply.
competitors.reporting: Real-time reporting and promotional tools are advertised.
competitors.gap: Reconcile cashback marketing language with the written pass-through restriction and publish account/instrument rates.
opportunities: Make the affiliate-to-client value proposition explicit and publish a compliant cashback/pass-through policy.
Use the existing real-time tools to provide partner-facing retention alerts and campaign diagnostics.
Reduce the barrier to small affiliates by testing lower-frequency or more flexible payout operations where commercially safe.
risks: A weekly cycle and USD 500 threshold can make the programme feel slower than daily or same-day competitors.
Unresolved cashback wording can make affiliates hesitant to promote the offer.
Headline USD/lot comparisons are not comparable without account, instrument, tier and eligibility rules.

competitors.label: HFM
competitors.headline: Up to USD 30 / lot
competitors.japan: Japanese pages, but international-use disclaimer leaves Japan eligibility unresolved
competitors.economics: Official partner pages advertise up to USD 30/lot and 60% revenue share.
competitors.rebate: Official FAQ supports automatic rebates; no official client pass-through rate was identified.
competitors.payout: Daily payments and withdrawal from USD 5 are advertised; the complete binding schedule was not identified.
competitors.restrictions: Pre-registration trades are excluded; account registration and approval are required.
competitors.gap: Confirm Japan/entity eligibility and obtain the binding affiliate agreement.
competitors.classification: Primary claim; secondary market rates excluded from headline
opportunities: Position XMTD on Japan certainty and documentation completeness rather than only headline commission.
Benchmark partner analytics and daily payout communication against the HFM claim set.
risks: The USD 30/lot and 60% claims may be perceived as stronger by affiliates even though Japan applicability is unresolved.
Secondary market cashback sources can influence perception outside the official partner programme.

competitors.label: Exness
competitors.headline: 20–40% spread share / fixed lot
competitors.basis: Spread-share or fixed per lot by account and tier
competitors.japan: Japanese official help centre with regional/global rules; entity agreement remains open
competitors.economics: Standard and Standard Cent: 20–40% average spread by tier; Pro: 17–25%; Zero and Raw: fixed per lot by instrument and tier.
competitors.rebate: Partners can share up to 100% of their reward; client/group rates and daily, weekly or monthly schedules are configurable. Copy Trading is excluded.
competitors.payout: Daily or instant partner rewards; instant reward may arrive within about 20 minutes. Client rebates can be daily, weekly or monthly.
competitors.restrictions: Self-referral, bonus-only, suspicious activity, cancelled spike trades and zero-volume orders are excluded.
competitors.reporting: API, AppsFlyer/postback, customizable links and reports updated about every ten minutes.
competitors.gap: Confirm the entity-specific Japan agreement and final regional rate schedule.
opportunities: Match the clarity of account/tier mechanics and give affiliates a calculator for expected reward and client rebate.
Improve retention through near-real-time reporting, event callbacks and client-level rebate controls where compliant.
risks: The combination of fast rewards, configurable client sharing and API reporting raises the switching cost for affiliates.
Third-party Japanese cashback providers create an established market expectation around speed and direct-to-account value.

competitors.label: Vantage
competitors.headline: Up to USD 12 / lot
competitors.economics: Four ranks. Standard FX: USD 4/6/8/10; oil, gold and silver: USD 6/8/10/12; ECN FX/metals: USD 0.5/1/1.5/2.
competitors.rebate: Standard client cashback pass-through rate was not identified. Separate IB-specific client promotions exist.
competitors.payout: Next-day reward credit; USD/JPY and bank, crypto or BitWallet withdrawal methods.
competitors.restrictions: Standard/ECN trades under three minutes, bonus-funded trades and self-affiliate activity are excluded; additional-account rules apply.
competitors.reporting: Partner portal and reporting; two-tier sub-IB structure; additional accounts covered.
competitors.gap: Confirm current application availability and resolve the rank-adjustment rule conflict.
opportunities: Give affiliates a simpler, instrument-aware rate card and calculator with fewer interpretation steps.
Use Japan certainty and a clear pass-through policy to differentiate from the unresolved rebate layer.
risks: The visible rank matrix can make the programme easier to explain than XMTD's headline-only presentation.
Conflicting rank/application information creates a reminder that all competitor claims need refresh validation.

competitors.label: XS.com
competitors.headline: Rate not found
competitors.japan: Japanese affiliate page; loyalty terms are global and Japan applicability is unconfirmed
competitors.economics: A numeric commission rate was not identified in the reviewed first-party sources.
competitors.rebate: Trader cashback/pass-through was not identified in the reviewed first-party sources.
competitors.payout: Same-day wallet payment is stated on the digital affiliate page; minimum withdrawal was not identified.
competitors.restrictions: Detailed Japan-specific affiliate restrictions were not established.
competitors.reporting: Real-time reporting and marketing tools are stated.
competitors.gap: Obtain the Japan-specific affiliate agreement. GAP-001 is open and high priority.
opportunities: Monitor loyalty milestones and retention mechanics as a non-rate competitor signal.
Win on transparent Japan-specific documentation and measurable partner support.
risks: A loyalty-led proposition can retain high-value partners even without public numeric rates.
The open Japan agreement makes direct comparison incomplete.

opportunities.title: Clarify the client-value promise
opportunities.detail: Publish a Japan-specific explanation of whether, when and how affiliate earnings can be passed through to clients, aligned to the agreement and approval process.

opportunities.title: Reduce payout friction
opportunities.detail: Assess a lower minimum or more frequent payout path for eligible affiliates, while preserving fraud and cost controls.

opportunities.title: Make economics calculable
opportunities.detail: Add account, instrument, volume-tier and client-rebate scenarios so affiliates can compare expected value without relying on a headline maximum.

opportunities.title: Operationalise retention analytics
opportunities.detail: Expose partner-level reporting, campaign attribution and an alert loop for inactive, high-value or at-risk affiliates.

risks.title: Pass-through ambiguity
risks.detail: Marketing copy can be read more broadly than the agreement. This creates compliance, trust and affiliate-activation risk.

risks.title: Non-comparable headline rates
risks.detail: USD/lot, revenue share, spread share and fixed commissions depend on different account, instrument, tier and eligibility bases.

risks.title: Japan entity uncertainty
risks.detail: Some competitor evidence is Japan-facing but still references global or international rules; entity-specific agreements remain missing.

risks.title: Market cashback expectations
risks.detail: Japanese third-party providers promote direct-to-account, next-day or high-pass-through mechanics that may shape affiliate expectations.

rules: Do not treat not found as not offered.
Keep Japan applicability separate from global or international evidence.
Show source IDs and refresh dates.
Do not create an overall ranking when bases are not comparable.
